parameters.query:
-- Instantly fact. A send is not a stage change; this row is the timestamped observation.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
insert into events (lead_id, lead_email, actor, action, outcome, workflow, units, est_cost_usd, payload)
select (select id from leads where vio_canon(contact_email::text) = vio_canon(p.j->>'lead_email')),
       coalesce(p.j->>'lead_email', ''),
       'instantly',
       coalesce(p.j->>'action', ''),
       coalesce(p.j->>'result', ''),
       'VIO-instantly-events',
       coalesce(nullif(p.j->>'units', '')::numeric, 1),
       null,
       jsonb_build_object('campaign', p.j->>'campaign')
from p
returning id

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ lead_email: $json.lead_email || '', action: $json.action || '', result: $json.result || '', units: $json.units, campaign: $json.campaign || '' }) }}

parameters.query:
-- After suppression. Unknown addresses update zero rows; the suppress insert still happened.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
update leads l set
  channel_state_email = (p.j->>'channel_state_email')::vio_email_state,
  updated_at = now()
from p
where vio_canon(l.contact_email::text) = vio_canon(p.j->>'contact_email')
  and p.j->>'channel_state_email' in ('bounced', 'unsubscribed')
returning l.id, l.contact_email, l.channel_state_email

-- Bounce / opt-out first. If the process dies after this insert, the address is
-- already blocked and only the lead row looks stale — that is the safe half.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
insert into suppression (identifier_type, identifier_value, reason, added_by)
select (p.j->>'identifier_type')::vio_identifier_type,
       p.j->>'identifier_value',
       coalesce(p.j->>'reason', ''),
       coalesce(p.j->>'added_by', 'VIO-instantly-events')
from p
returning id
